newsitem.title: CHINA: China market for larger cars seen up 32 pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: China market for larger cars seen up 32 pct in '97.

text.p: The Chinese market for mid-sized and large cars is expected to surge by about 32 percent in 1997 to 45,000 vehicles from 34,000 in 1996, the China Daily said on Thursday.
Demand would grow to 96,000 cars in 1998 and 135,000 in 2000, the newspaper quoted Chen Ping, vice president of the China Trade Centre for Imported Automobiles, as saying.
It gave no details of the classes of car that would be in most demand but said many of the 125,000 mid-sized passenger cars in China were old and needed to be replaced.
Demand for larger cars had been boosted by a 1996 crackdown on vehicle smuggling and unauthorised barter trading of foreign cars, it said.
It added adding joint venture producers were gearing up to produce domestic cars to undercut highly-priced imports.
